properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"An epoch can be planned, not only recorded","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"The temporal axis must run forward as well as back, in TWO PAIRED VIEWS of the same architecture (Anthony, 2026-07-28: 'in systems engineering, I think this would be 2 views of the same system'): increments in TIME — epochs, what the architecture is expected to be at epoch_1..n — and increments in CAPABILITY — what each small, frequent release adds, the release-fast-in-small-increments practice now common in industry (his brother's project ships ~2 minor releases a week). Both views must exist, each comparable as a delta: any two epochs, any two increments, or either against the present. With many moving parts — an ecosystem of coupled repos, each with its own graph — an epoch or increment must pin the set of per-repo design versions it means, or the question 'which epoch are we talking about?' has no answer, which is the failure this exists to prevent. Original idea 2026-07-28 ('epoch branches: project_x:epoch_1 captures what we expect the graph to look like at epoch_1'), amended the same day with the two-views framing. THE ATOM, Anthony's distillation 2026-07-28: the roadmap is a SATISFACTION SCHEDULE — a mapping of requirements to the epoch or increment where they are satisfied: 'in epoch 1, requirements A and B are satisfied; in increment 3, requirements C, D and E are expected to be satisfied; in epoch 27, KPP 1 is required to be satisfied.' His own verbs carry the three modalities the mapping must distinguish: ARE satisfied (recorded history — the backward direction the graph already does), EXPECTED to be satisfied (a plan, carrying confidence that decays with horizon per req:plans-move-honestly), and REQUIRED to be satisfied by (an obligation whose miss at arrival is a computed violation, the scheduling face of a KPP — content inviolability from req:inviolable-intent gains a deadline dimension).","status":"accepted"}
